venue: Student Union Ballroom, U. of Utah

songs.name: He Was A Friend Of Mine

ai_show_review.summary: Dark Star, The Eleven & Lovelight blaze a classic ’69 set
ai_show_review.blurb: The show delivers powerful Dark Star and an incendiary The Eleven, with a fiery Lovelight that cuts through the analog hiss. Jerry’s guitar is aggressive despite a restless crowd, while Bob adds his trademark humor between jams.
ai_show_review.review: On April 12, 1969 at the Student Union Ballroom in Salt Lake City the Dead rolled out an early‑show set that still feels vivid today. A strong Dark Star launches the second half into deep, exploratory terrain, leading into a thunderous The Eleven and a blazing Lovelight that proves to be the night’s high point. Jerry Garcia plays with a bite, his tone cutting through the classic analog hiss of the soundboard tape while he battles an audience that isn’t quite ready to dance. Bob Weir peppers the set with oddball jokes – the infamous Yellow Dog story – keeping the mood loose as the band weaves between tight jams and experimental detours. Though the recording suffers from a few splices, pitch‑correction quirks and missing portions of The Other One and Too, the remaining material captures the restless energy and improvisational spirit that defined the Dead in ’69.

best_recording.reason: Soundboard source with classic analog hiss; most complete tape despite a few splices and missing cuts.

key_highlights: Lovelight – fiery climax of the set
song_highlights: He Was A Friend Of Mine

band_performance.Jerry: Agitated by a non‑dancing crowd yet delivers strong guitar tone and energetic playing.
band_performance.Bob: Adds oddball character with Yellow Dog jokes that pepper the performance.
